name: Navigation App
description: An entry on the navigation rail: a named group of sidebars. The rail lists these first; every sidebar none of them claims is still reachable, grouped under the installed app it belongs to.

fields.label: Title
fields.description: What the rail's tooltip and the sidebar header call this app.

fields.label: Enabled
fields.description: A disabled app is left off the rail and claims none of its sidebars, so they fall back to the installed apps they belong to.

fields.label: Rail Order
fields.description: Lower numbers sit higher on the rail. Ties are broken by title.

fields.label: Icon
fields.description: Drawn on the rail when there is no logo.

fields.label: Logo
fields.description: Drawn on the rail in place of the icon.

fields.label: Sidebars
fields.description: The modules this app offers. The rail and the sidebar's top menu always list them alphabetically, by label. A sidebar can belong to only one enabled app.

fields.label: Frontend URL
fields.description: An app with a frontend of its own, outside the desk, such as /helpdesk or /commons. Offered beside the app's modules and opened in the same tab. An app with a frontend and no sidebars opens it straight from the rail.

fields.label: Frontend Label
fields.description: What the module list and the top menu call the frontend. Left blank, the app's title followed by "app".

fields.label: Roles
fields.description: Only people with one of these roles see the app on the rail. Left empty, everyone does. Either way, a sidebar a person cannot open is not offered to them.
